A day for each feast

Saturnalia

A Day of Saturnalian Merriment at Home

Embrace the ancient Roman spirit of Saturnalia with a day dedicated to joy, feasting, and playful role reversal, right in your own home. It's a time to relax, share generously, and shout "Io Saturnalia!" with abandon.

  1. Morning

    Don Your Pileus!

    Begin your Saturnalian day by donning a felt pileus cap, a symbol of freedom and festivity. Greet your household with a hearty "Io Saturnalia!" to set the joyful tone.

  2. Late Morning

    Prepare the Grand Feast

    The heart of Saturnalia is the banquet. Start preparing your magnificent roast pork, allowing its aromas to fill your home and build anticipation for the evening's meal.

    Recipes: Saturnalia Roast Pork

  3. Afternoon

    Sweeten the Celebration

    While the main course cooks, prepare the traditional mulsum sweet wine and delightful honey cakes. These treats will add a touch of ancient Roman sweetness to your festivities.

    Recipes: Mulsum Sweet Wine · Saturnalia Honey Cakes

  4. Late Afternoon

    Games and Generosity

    Engage in playful games and exchange small, thoughtful gifts, embodying the generous spirit of Saturnalia. You might even elect a mock king to preside over the afternoon's fun.

  5. Evening

    The Saturnalian Banquet

    Gather for a lavish banquet, a cornerstone of the festival. Share plates piled high with roast pork, olives, and pine nuts, all accompanied by your homemade mulsum and honey cakes.

    Recipes: Saturnalia Roast Pork · Marinated Olives for Saturnalia · Mulsum Sweet Wine · Honey-Glazed Pine Nuts for Saturnalia · Saturnalia Honey Cakes

  6. After Dinner

    Lingering Merriment

    Continue the relaxed atmosphere, perhaps with more games or simply enjoying conversation and the lingering tastes of your feast, celebrating the temporary freedom from daily cares.

May your home be filled with laughter and abundance as you honor the spirit of Saturnalia.
